title: Armstrong's last dance, Sidney Desvigne's band and King Oliver
summary: Gabriel recalls Armstrong's farewell dance in 1923, playing drums in Sidney Desvigne's band, and King Oliver rehearsing with his father.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: And the last thing Louis played was a dance for my daddy at the Coliseum. I advertised, not the dance. He played the advertised. I played the clarinet. He left that same night in 1923. First time a dance was ever gave down there. But Sidney Dazman, he played the job. And I played with Sidney Dazman's band, two drums. He just came into me and I played the drum in the band. When I was playing the drum in the band, I was on the drum. Vic was on the tramo, Vic Gasper. And Sidney Dazman on the trumpet. The crew on the clarinet. Willie Vaughn 10 on the banjo. And Oak was on the bass. Is that six pieces? I think so. Well, that was that band I played with them. And when we played that high society, we had to get very low for Piku. And we played all those places around. I was a drum in that band. But Sidney was playing by himself in grown lady years. And he put up a big band where he could sit behind the axe and do nothing. But he used to play a nice trumpet. And Joe Oliver, when we would be rehearsing, he would come and rehearsing with my dad. He couldn't leave a number. King Oliver. He clubbed with a cataract now. You ever seen him? I know, but I was seeing the picture.
I know he had the one bad eye.
Yeah, well, alright. Well, he would be in the club. So after rehearsing with us a whole lot and playing a little round, Bruce the man was playing peck horn then.

He was a good trumpet player. And so he played. And Michael Perez taking him in the band. And after he got through the orchestra with Kid Orwell, he was fast. He always heard that monkey shine. And he went up the line. He sent him out of scrum. There was a whole lot of fellas around here that could play old time fellas. Such as, you know Suga? No. That was a time I wanted to play over the river. Jack Pyee? No.
